review.scope_assessment: This second, corrective-only review covers exactly the 8 files in the P5-F1 delta (apps/web/src/lib/booking-access-runtime.ts; docs/adr/0032-*.md; new packages/core/src/guest/booking-access-keys.ts; tests/flow/launcher.ts; tests/readiness/booking-recovery.ts; tests/readiness/production-rehearsal.ts; tests/readiness/rehearsal-server.ts; new tests/unit/booking-access-keys.test.ts), plus their necessary existing dependents (booking-access.ts, booking-recovery.ts, rental-flow.ts, migration 0024) needed to confirm the fix is wired consistently end-to-end. The prior LOW finding P5-F1 concerned BookingAccess and BookingRecovery being derived from one identical HMAC-SHA256 root key/keyVersion, relying only on distinct purpose-string prefixes inside the HMAC message for domain separation. The fix introduces deriveBookingAccessKeys(master), which derives two structurally independent 32-byte subkeys via HMAC-SHA256(master, distinct-label) — an accessKey under the unchanged P4 label ('zao-owned-development-booking-access-v1', preserving byte-for-byte P4 compatibility, confirmed by the fixed-vector unit test) and a recoveryKey under a new distinct label ('zao-owned-development-booking-recovery-root-v1'). Every call site that previously shared one key (runtime, test launcher, readiness booking-recovery test, production-rehearsal, rehearsal-server) was updated consistently to pass accessKey to BookingAccess and recoveryKey to BookingRecovery, with recovery additionally using new distinct keyVersion strings ('development-recovery-v1' / 'rehearsal-recovery-v1') layered on top of the key separation. The new unit test directly reproduces the previously-failing structural property (HMAC under accessKey vs recoveryKey over an identical accidental message must differ) and the supplied before/after counterexample logs show it failing pre-fix and passing post-fix; both this test and the full P4/P5 recovery/rehearsal/UI/real-PostgreSQL regression suites pass in both local-verification and the fresh exact-head CI run (34774399526, conclusion success, integration_parents/head/base/tree all matching the stated base/head). No secret storage, credential handling, DB roles/grants, permissions, price/HOLD/business rules, or unrelated code were touched by this delta. I independently confirm P5-F1 is resolved as a real, tested fix rather than a documentation-only claim; this remains a static, non-executing confirmation and does not constitute production authorization, external provider acceptance, or merge permission — all B-H areas and external/Owner gates are unchanged from the first full review's baseline and are not re-litigated here.

findings.condition: BookingAccess and BookingRecovery are both constructed from the identical HMAC-SHA256 root key and identical keyVersion label; domain separation between the two capability classes relies solely on distinct purpose-string prefixes embedded inside each JSON-serialized HMAC message, not on independently derived root keys.
findings.impact: Reduces cryptographic defense-in-depth: since both the confirmed-booking read capability (BookingAccess) and the recovery code/recovered-read token (BookingRecovery) are HMACed under one shared secret, any future bug that causes a purpose-string collision or an unescaped/ambiguous value in the JSON.stringify-based domain-separation input could let a token minted for one capability be reproduced or confused with the other. Today the purpose strings ('zao-booking-read-v1' vs 'zao-booking-recovery-v1' vs 'zao-booking-recovered-read-v1') are distinct and non-colliding, so no live exploit exists, but the shared-key design removes the structural guarantee that would otherwise make such a future mistake cryptographically inert.
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/booking-access-runtime.ts:17-18: `const key=createHmac('sha256',p.r.config.authSecret).update('zao-owned-development-booking-access-v1').digest(); return {p,access:new BookingAccess(pool,key,'development-v1'),recovery:new BookingRecovery(pool,key,'development-v1')};` — the same `key` and `'development-v1'` version string are passed into both `new BookingAccess(...)` (packages/core/src/guest/booking-access.ts) and `new BookingRecovery(...)` (packages/core/src/guest/booking-recovery.ts).
findings.fix: Derive two independent root keys from authSecret with distinct labels, e.g. `createHmac('sha256',authSecret).update('zao-booking-access-root-v1').digest()` for BookingAccess and a separate `...update('zao-booking-recovery-root-v1').digest()` for BookingRecovery, so a future purpose-string mistake in one component cannot be leveraged against the other.
findings.test: Add a unit test that constructs BookingAccess and BookingRecovery from the same authSecret via bookingAccessRuntime-equivalent derivation and asserts their effective per-purpose HMAC outputs are independent (i.e., that the runtime derives non-identical key material for the two components), failing today since both currently receive the exact same 32-byte key.
